clue.text: Frisk doctor in prison

indicators.note: one thing placed in another sits inside it, so the doctor goes within the prison word

blocks.note: gaol is the British spelling of jail
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A doctor working in a prison is told to search an inmate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frisk' looks like a search by a guard, but here it means to leap about playfully: GA(MB)OL.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are verbs for skipping and leaping about playfully, like lambs in spring.

clue.text: A bishop on an island

blocks.note: taken as written
RR, Right Reverend, is the title of a bishop
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bishop is posted to a remote island parish.
explanation.walkthrough: Arran is a Scottish island in the Firth of Clyde.
explanation.definitionFit: Arran is a large island off the west coast of Scotland, so it is an example of an island.

clue.text: Handle carriages, so some say, with credit

indicators.note: what some people say is heard rather than read, so the carriages are taken by their sound

blocks.note: broughams are horse-drawn carriages, pronounced like sweeping brushes
on tick is British slang for on credit

explanation.surface: Someone is told to deal with carriages bought on credit.
explanation.walkthrough: A brougham is a closed four-wheeled horse carriage; the word is said 'broom'. 'Handle' looks like a verb but is the noun: the long handle of a broom.
explanation.definitionFit: A broomstick is the long wooden pole of a broom, the part you hold, so it is a handle.

clue.text: Wrecker did, maliciously breaking instrument

indicators.note: something done maliciously is done destructively, so these letters are wrecked into a new order
breaking into something means getting inside it, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: a lute is a stringed musical instrument
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A vandal maliciously smashed a musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: The Luddites were 19th-century English textile workers who smashed machinery, so the word now means anyone who opposes new technology.
explanation.definitionFit: The original Luddites wrecked weaving machines, so a Luddite is a machine-wrecker.

clue.text: Offshoot of British farm

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for British
a ranch is a large farm, especially for cattle

explanation.surface: A spin-off business grows out of a British farm.
explanation.definitionFit: A branch is a limb growing out of a tree trunk, or a division of an organisation: an offshoot either way.

clue.text: Bird from intensely cold North

blocks.note: a bitter wind is intensely cold
N is the abbreviation for North

explanation.surface: A bird has flown down from the freezing north.
explanation.definitionFit: The bittern is a shy wading bird of the heron family, known for its booming call.

clue.text: A leader of men, very large man

indicators.note: the leader of a group goes in front, so only the opening letter of the following word is kept

blocks.note: taken as written
the opening letter of men
OS stands for outsize, the clothing size for very large

explanation.surface: A towering figure leads his men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A leader of men' reads as a description of a commander, but it is three separate pieces; 'man' alone is the definition, a figure from the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: Amos was an Old Testament prophet, so he is a man in the sense crosswords use for any named male.

clue.text: Leader one English newspaper printed during row

indicators.note: something printed during a run appears in the middle of it, so these pieces go inside the outer word

blocks.note: a chain is a connected row or series
I is the Roman numeral for one
E is the abbreviation for English
the FT is the Financial Times, a British newspaper

explanation.surface: A leader article in an English paper is printed in the middle of a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' suggests a quarrel, but it is a line of linked things: CH(I E FT)AIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A chieftain is the head of a clan or tribe, so a leader.

clue.text: Fancy icing in tandoori? Restaurant may have it

indicators.note: fancy means elaborate or ornamental, so the letters that follow are dressed up into a new arrangement

blocks.note: all fifteen letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether an Indian restaurant's tandoori comes with decorative icing.
explanation.walkthrough: The tandoor is a hot clay oven, so the restaurant's cooling system is a neat contrast with the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Air conditioning is a cooling system that many restaurants install, so it is something one may have.

clue.text: Saying not applicable to a busman's holiday?

annotation.answer: A CHANGE IS AS GOOD AS A REST

definitions.text: Saying not applicable to a busman's holiday?

blocks.clueFragment: Saying not applicable to a busman's holiday?
blocks.note: surface reading: some proverb that does not suit a bus driver's time off
setter's reading: a busman's holiday is a break spent doing the same as one's job, so it offers no variety, and the proverb that praises variety cannot apply

explanation.walkthrough: A busman's holiday is a British idiom for leisure time spent doing the same thing as your work, like a bus driver taking a coach trip.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says that variety refreshes as well as rest does, which is exactly what a busman's holiday lacks.

clue.text: See 8 down
Old servant given cards first

blocks.note: a hand is the set of cards a player holds
a maiden voyage or speech is the first one

explanation.surface: A long-serving servant is dealt cards before anyone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cards first' reads as dealing order, but 'first' is its own piece, as in a maiden flight.
explanation.definitionFit: Handmaiden is an archaic word for a female personal servant or maid.

clue.text: Hairstyle sported by Doctor Faustus, swept back

indicators.note: something sported by a person is worn on them, so the letters sit inside the following words
swept back, like hair, means turned the other way, so the letters are read from right to left

blocks.note: the letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: Marlowe's Doctor Faustus wears his hair combed backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer straddles doctOR FAustus and must be read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An Afro is a rounded, bushy style of naturally tightly curled hair.

clue.text: Dreadful August riot, uncalled for

indicators.note: something dreadful is in a terrible state, so the letters that follow are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: all ten letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Commentators call a terrible summer riot unprovoked.
explanation.definitionFit: Gratuitous means without good reason or justification, so it is a synonym of uncalled for.

clue.text: Loose thing that is worn in bed?

definitions.text: Loose thing that is worn in bed?

blocks.clueFragment: Loose thing that is worn in bed?
blocks.note: surface reading: something slack or untied found in the bed
setter's reading: a loose-fitting garment that one puts on to sleep in; 'that is' also hints at IE as an ending

explanation.walkthrough: 'Loose' suggests something come adrift, but it describes a baggy garment; the phrase 'that is' quietly echoes the letters IE closing the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightie is a loose nightdress worn by women and girls for sleeping.

clue.text: Awfully daring, he's decorated

indicators.note: something done awfully is done badly, so the letters that follow are scrambled

blocks.note: all nine letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man is honoured with a medal for extreme bravery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decorated' suggests a medal for daring, but it is food dressed with a garnish.
explanation.definitionFit: To garnish is to decorate a dish with small trimmings, so garnished means decorated.

clue.text: Driving vehicle through pouring rain is bliss?

indicators.note: rain that is pouring is tumbling down in a rush, so its letters spill into a new order
one thing passing through another is inside it, so the vehicle sits within the rearranged letters

blocks.note: a van is a vehicle that is driven
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A driver asks whether motoring through a downpour can really be called bliss.
explanation.definitionFit: Nirvana is the Buddhist state of perfect peace, and loosely any state of perfect happiness.

clue.text: A complaint is made by each girl left out

indicators.note: left out tells us the letter standing for left is dropped from the name

blocks.note: ea. is the abbreviation for each
a girl's name

explanation.surface: A grievance arises because every girl has been excluded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left out' reads as excluded, but it means remove L (left) from the name: EA + RACHE(L).
explanation.definitionFit: Earache is a pain in the ear, and complaint here is the medical sense of an ailment.

clue.text: Perfect example in opening to Exodus (religious book)

indicators.note: the opening of a book is its first page, so only the initial letter of the next word is kept

blocks.note: the opening letter of Exodus
pi is short for pious, so religious
a tome is a large book

explanation.surface: A perfect illustration is found at the start of Exodus, a religious book.
explanation.walkthrough: PI, from pious, is a crossword favourite for religious.
explanation.definitionFit: An epitome is a person or thing that perfectly typifies a class or quality.

clue.text: Building that's spherical — amphitheatre, originally

indicators.note: originally points to how a word begins, so just its first letter is kept

blocks.note: rotund means round or plump
the initial letter of amphitheatre

explanation.surface: A round building is described as having started life as an amphitheatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Building that's spherical' looks like one definition, but only 'Building' defines; 'spherical' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotunda is a round building, typically one topped by a dome.

clue.text: Great at new sporting event

indicators.note: something new has been made afresh, so the letters before it are remade in another order

blocks.note: all seven letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone excels at a newly introduced sport.
explanation.definitionFit: A regatta is a series of boat or yacht races, so it is a sporting occasion.

clue.text: Head of soccer outfit in comedy sketch

indicators.note: the head of anything is its top, so only the opening letter of the next word is kept

blocks.note: the opening letter of soccer
a football team's kit is its outfit

explanation.surface: A football club boss appears in costume in a comic sketch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head of soccer outfit' reads as a club manager, but 'outfit' means clothing, not a team.
explanation.definitionFit: A skit is a short comic piece of theatre, a synonym of comedy sketch.

clue.text: Page written about the Italian forbidding a journey to a shrine

indicators.note: something written about other words is wrapped around them, so the page goes outside

blocks.note: taken as written
il is Italian for the
a grim look is forbidding

explanation.surface: A page is written about a grim Italian, nodding to a journey to a holy site.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forbidding' looks like a verb meaning banning, but here it is the adjective for stern and menacing.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilgrimage is a journey made to a sacred place for religious reasons.

clue.text: There's fury when old car fails to start

indicators.note: failing to start means missing the beginning, so the first letter of the word is dropped

blocks.note: a banger is British slang for an old, rickety car

explanation.surface: A driver is furious when his old car won't start.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a banger is a battered old car.
explanation.definitionFit: Anger and fury are synonyms for strong displeasure.

clue.text: Guru's student in Tokyo — girl

indicators.note: in says the letters lie inside the following words, running across them

blocks.note: the letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: A guru has a pupil who is a girl living in Tokyo.
explanation.definitionFit: A yogi is a practitioner of yoga, typically one learning under a guru's guidance.

clue.text: Where Plato was taught a lesson?

definitions.text: Where Plato was taught a lesson?

blocks.clueFragment: Where Plato was taught a lesson?
blocks.note: surface reading: the place where the philosopher sat in class
setter's reading: a philosopher belongs to a body of shared philosophical ideas, a group named after its way of reasoning rather than a building

explanation.walkthrough: 'Taught a lesson' suggests a classroom, but the answer is a philosophical movement; Plato learned from Socrates and founded his own Academy.
explanation.definitionFit: A school of thought is a group sharing a particular philosophy, which is where a thinker like Plato belongs.

clue.text: Respect shown by upright character in strange dream

indicators.note: something strange is out of the ordinary, so the letters of the next word come out of order
in places the upright character inside the jumbled word

blocks.note: the capital I is a single upright stroke
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: An honest person earns respect by appearing in someone's odd dream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upright character' suggests a person of integrity; it is the letter I, a single vertical stroke.
explanation.definitionFit: To admire someone is to hold them in high regard, so to respect them.

clue.text: Buds are almost out — that's ridiculous

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter of the second word is dropped
out suggests things put out of place, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
the word without its final letter

explanation.surface: A gardener scoffs at buds nearly opening so early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out' looks like the buds blooming, but it signals a rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Absurd and ridiculous are synonyms for wildly unreasonable or laughable.
